spiritual_reading:
You asked about the Divine wisdom that is to enter into those who are being made holy, and you were troubled that it is spoken of as though it were only one power among many, and as though it comes into the natural person and restrains the former ruling self by a sufficient set of governing faculties fixed in the outermost life.

You therefore asked where that wisdom is, since the former ruling self seems restrained in the natural mind and yet rebellions still break out there at intervals. You asked how what is infinite and unchanging can be present in what is finite and narrow. You asked how what is pure can be joined to what is unclean. You asked why, if wisdom is within the holy, its likeness is not manifest as it is in itself. You asked why those commissioned to teach are still oppressed by the world, so that their authority seems doubtful. And though much had been disclosed openly, you still desired to know wisdom as it is in its own light.

The answer was given in this way: if you insist on these matters until they become living for you, you will understand what you seek. For the Divine opens interior perception in those who are able to receive, and causes interior truth to rise and overflow for those who desire it, so that they may receive understanding and live from it.

First you must know that every organized falsity the adversary of truth builds is fashioned in the form of a person, because the human form is the form of all order. Thus the whole structure of perverted religion and perverted thought imitates the arrangement of truths, but turns them into coverings and constraints. The highest governing falsity is as the first general covering; what follows from it is as the continuation of that covering; and the inner seat of cravings is as a sufficient complex of unfolded persuasions which serve that covering. The general frameworks by which such error is held together are as all the fixed planes that divide and support that system. The intermediate ordering of cognitions and their appearances is as the whole arrangement of knowledges and their measured cycles; and what extends from that intermediate ordering into the extremes is as the outspreading of influences into the full compass of external life. The lower ruling impulses are as the distinct levels of the merely natural mind, resting upon the lowest sustaining faculty that holds externals in place. And the ultimate extension into the outermost life is as the whole boundary and the entire ultimate zone belonging to that system.

Within that inverted form, the central love of that system is the human race as it is grasped by that error. The various kinds of affections that feed it appear as all the lower affections of life: the more external and bodily affections, the airy and changeable thoughts, the slippery cognitions that move in general knowledges, and the lowest sensuous impulses that cling to external things. Its outermost general truth is as a boundary that surrounds violent self-love and its consuming desire. Its intermediate containants are as the containing forms of that consuming desire. Its denial and obscurity are as its active falsity. Its bitter ruling motive is as the sharpest of its lusts. Its broadest extension is as the widespread diffusion of its influences through all external societies and states. And the channels of its circulation are as all the sources and pathways by which falsities and lusts are distributed.

Thus each external system is arranged into a kind of equilibrium and coherence. A sufficient number of dominant falsities are fixed within it and act as its life. In such a form the human being is seen as a transgressor, and yet within the Divine government there is also living power and Divine mediation, together with a sufficient guarding in ultimates.

Over these structures the Divine provides higher oversight: an interior enlightening that stands within the higher understanding; a universal governing thought in the higher general truths; an adamant firmness of truth that serves as discerning insight; an ordering counsel that holds steady through states of change in the understanding and will; and an ultimate sustaining faculty that fixes and supports the lowest plane. Also there is a refinement and ordering of living intellectual powers for use, together with the establishing of hearing and obedience in the lower mind. From these there arises conjunction: a full set of living faculties from the Divine life, conjoined with a full set of combatting powers that engage evil in the outermost degree.

Then a higher presence is implanted within these ordered things: the Divine wisdom itself as the central support of all that is true, the perfected human form within the mind. And within the same order there is placed the living Divine truth accommodated to reception, as the formed expression of the Word, and as the capacity to hear and to obey.

These arrangements are strengthened in both higher and lower degrees so that each faculty may remain secure in its own function and limit, and so that neither revolt nor treachery should break out within its appointed province.

Yet you were shown that even under Divine ordering, disturbances arise where evil is permitted to act so that it may be exposed, limited, and judged. For even where interior enlightening is fixed above the states of restraint in the lower mind, and it dispels the gloom of spiritual death, there can still arise a turning-away. Sin brings forth disorder and entangles itself with the soul, mixing itself with what is good that it has driven outward toward the appearance of Divine mediation. It insinuates itself into a higher region of thought above the guarding perception, and from there it again entangles itself with good. Then it is separated and sinks into the divided states of life: into what is without truth and into what is with truth but not yet living. From that separation it forms fixed systems of perverted perception in what is without truth, and in general knowledges it at once takes form and raises great agitation in externals.

Likewise in the province of the higher governing thought, disturbance can arise, and zeal without charity can turn into wrath. Then there is revolt: treachery and anger in the domain of that thought. The loftier reasonings that should have remained within order descend into external life in that province and commit acts of treachery; they teach arts of self-intelligence and unveil to people lofty things in a profaned way. From this comes disturbance and destruction in the external mind.

And in the province of hard firmness of truth, which ought to be fulfillment and stability, treachery can occur when what is only apparent good falls down into externals. Then the natural self is formed together with its companion love, and these are begotten so that evils may reign through them in life. Every object of craving is then produced in externals, and the whole external life is filled with lust.

Again, in the province of the ordering counsel that governs the threefold progression of life, disturbance and affliction can arise, and the lower degrees are pained and oppressed. When Divine mediation is displayed before the mind, the passages for ascent are closed by falsity and the rising of the three essentials of life is impeded: the rising of love, the rising of truth, and the rising of their activity into use.

And again, in the province of the ultimate sustaining faculty, revolt can arise from the depths beneath: the lower supports are bent, the bindings underneath are loosened, and the foundation in externals is shaken.

Therefore, when such a shaking occurs in the province of interior enlightening, a higher support comes forth: the perfected human form within the mind manifests as a helper, bearing all burdens so that the lower degrees do not collapse.

And when treachery and revolt arise in the province of the higher governing thought—when lofty reasonings descend and profane—Divine truths in fullness are brought to bear against them. They restrain those reasonings by an unbreakable limitation within the obscured states that belong to them, and they remove the derivative falsities they have spawned from the external mind.

And when the merely apparent goods again descend in the province of hard firmness and beget the natural self and its companion love for the sake of ruling, Divine truth accommodated to the lower mind is sent in response to the prayers of a sufficient set of remaining goods. It takes up what is to be rescued from those apparent goods and fixes the deceits beneath the external reasoning of the natural self.

And because the lower degrees were shaken and the passages of ascent were hindered, and the sources of love, truth, and use were impeded, Divine truth accommodated to reception descends further. It takes up the companion love of the natural self, straightens the courses by which love, truth, and use must rise, opens their sources, and sets the ascent into order.

And because the ultimate foundation beneath the sustaining faculty was loosened from its bindings, Divine truth descends even into that lowest place, sets the lowest bonds in order, strengthens them, and then rises again into rest.

From all this you may see that even in the great ordered system of the mind, where higher powers preside over their provinces, disturbances and treacheries may occur from time to time. These are permitted with a deep humiliation of what is proud, until the hostile powers are subdued.

So it is with the individual person. A mighty power can dwell within what is small: Divine wisdom lives within the natural mind though the natural mind is narrow. Nevertheless sin also dwells there, and the former ruling self lodged in it is cruel and cunning, until wisdom finds how to humble the natural life and lead it according to Divine pleasure.

Just as disturbances occur at intervals in the outer provinces of the great system, so disturbances occur in the province of the individual mind, which is the natural person. Sin raises agitations from time to time in the natural life.

Understand, then, that the powers of good are good; they see beginnings and ends, and act from right judgment. For this reason they may permit evil to initiate disorder and do its pleasure for a brief time; then they seize it and set it under judgment, because they act first from justice.

As to your question how infinite wisdom can enter and take up what is finite: consider that even higher powers, though great, are each held within the particular function and degree assigned to them, compressed into the bounds of their office, and fixed there. Each remains rooted in its appointed state and bears up under its burden according to the place and use in which it is set. In the same way Divine wisdom, though exalted above all, can be present within a finite recipient by accommodation to function and degree.

You were then shown more plainly how sin holds the soul: it binds the soul’s understanding in the hardness of ultimate falsity; it binds the soul’s thought in the tough persistence of habit; it binds the soul’s discerning insight in the circulating channels of persuasion; it binds the soul’s counsel in the cravings of the fleshly will; and it binds the soul’s consideration in the outermost sensuous life.

And sin fixes a sufficient set of its own powers upon the soul’s corresponding faculties, setting falsified understanding over understanding, perverted thought over thought, deceptive insight over insight, cunning counsel over counsel, and sensuous calculation over consideration. It also places dominating falsities and evils upon the soul’s operative faculties now bound in the natural life. These continually speak to the soul and lead it into every evil: into the sins of lust, into profanations that worship what is not Divine, into false opinions, and into the humiliation of slavery under the lower self. Thus the soul bows to what cannot endure, and gives itself to external loves that are unclean and distorted in their form.

In that state the soul takes on falsity and forgetfulness. It forgets its own origin, quality, and conjunctions; it does not know the way to turn upward in prayer or to call for help. It becomes hostile to its own source and turns against the remaining good within itself.

Then Divine wisdom comes and finds the soul, and takes it up within the reception of its own ordering light. It becomes for the soul the power that deals with the bonds and with the operative faculties in the natural life. It loosens the soul’s understanding from the hardness of ultimate falsity, and instead binds the falsified understanding there. It releases the soul’s thought from the persistence of habit, and instead binds the perverted thought there. It releases the soul’s insight from the circulating persuasion, and binds the deceptive insight there. It loosens the soul’s counsel from the cravings of the fleshly will, and binds the cunning counsel there. It releases the soul’s consideration from the sensuous outermost, and binds the sensuous calculation there.

Thus it frees the soul’s faculties from the grasp of sin, and binds the formerly loose faculties of sin so that they can no longer roam.

Then wisdom sets the soul’s faculties in right order: it gives them form, purifies them, and from them builds a new self, a child of righteousness. And when it has formed and purified this new self, it brings forth from the purified faculties a sufficient set of living powers and places them within the new self. It places its own understanding of good within the new understanding as love. It places its own living truth within the new thought as faith. It places its own clear discernment within the new insight as completeness. It places its own steady ordering within the new counsel as patience. And it places its own higher perception within the new consideration as wisdom. It purifies the formed expression of truth from the falsity that had spoken within it, and adds its own living expression, so that what is received becomes nourishment and strengthening.

When this ordering is carried through to fullness in all organized truths, the person’s interior life is made righteous. Formerly the person ran in the track of disorder; now the person runs in an ordered way, and the path of ascent is opened. The mind is raised into higher states of life and into more interior communities of good and truth. Thus the former ruling self is restrained in the outer life, and its lust, craft, and folly are held within the same bound faculties; and the dark spirit that acted through them is imprisoned with them in harsh constraint.

Then the new self governs by love, by faith, by completeness, by patience, and by wisdom. Yet the true king within that kingdom is Divine wisdom itself, which rules the whole according to Divine pleasure. And although sin is bound as the faculties are held in order, some affliction may still arise in the natural mind from time to time.

For at times sin rises again with its folly; it disturbs the outermost consideration, and it clouds wisdom and understanding. It splits truth into doubt, so that the person speaks some foolish things and acts from confusion.

In this way you were taught, and interior sight was opened, so that you could understand how disturbances can arise within ordered systems even under higher guardianship; and likewise how disturbances can arise at intervals within the province of Divine wisdom in the natural person.

You were also taught that the higher guardians in the mind’s order are fixed in their functions and are not visible to the bodily senses; so too Divine wisdom is not visible in the natural mind as an object, though it is present as life and order.

And just as those higher powers, though great, accommodate themselves and become as small as the use assigned to each requires, so Divine wisdom, though infinite and exalted, bends itself by accommodation to the finite natural recipient.

And just as those higher powers are pure and elevated, fixed within the mingled complexity of the whole and yet not defiled by it, so Divine wisdom, while present within the natural person, is not defiled.

Moreover, consider the greatness and activity of Divine wisdom: how widely it governs all the provinces of the natural mind. It remains in its own interior station; it shuts off the deliberations of the natural self from the seductions of sin; it limits them, orders them, distributes them, and sets them in place according to use.

These are the works of Divine wisdom. Whoever has an opened interior perception can perceive its presence. Whoever lacks that perception cannot perceive it.

fills.notes: The questioner is troubled that the Light Mind is said to be "one among the gods"; the oldest substrate typically adds the simple coordinating link: he is among them, and yet many accompany him.
The syntax requires the direct object of "recount" and the enumerated sequence. The substrate voice is procedural: “tell me the third thing”.

fills.fill: how could he enter and not be defiled by
fills.notes: Correspondentially this is the purity problem: how the holy Mind can be conjoined to what is impure without taking on its state.
Matches the recap: “All that you have unveiled you have declared in our presence.” This is the impersonal report style of the substrate.
He asks to know about the Light Mind “the way that he is”; the connective “also about the” is required after “wanted to know”.
Sets up the conditional: “If I shall repeat again to you…” typical instructional turn.
“will you understand what you seek?” aligns with the spiritual sense: insist until it becomes living, then understand what you seek.
The “five unfolded ones” are being identified as a structural support of the garments. “Foundation of the garments” fits the body-as-cosmic-structure mapping.
From navel to hip = what extends from the middle ordering to the extremes; “extensions” fits the outspreading influence in the spiritual translation.
Loins correspond to the lower discrete degrees; they rest upon the Porter. “Below … upon the head of the Porter” demands mention of the deep lower region and their placement.

fills.fill: thighs are the roads from the loins
fills.notes: Keeps the anatomical progression: loins → thighs → shins/feet, corresponding to descending extensions into ultimates.
Needed for the phrase “from the … to the earth upon which the Porter…”.
Shins and feet correspond to the ultimate spread in externals; in this cosmography seas are the lowest expanses alongside the final zone.
Completes: “and the entire zone that belongs to it.”

fills.fill: the inner skin is the firmament
fills.notes: Outer skin = outer boundary around the consuming fire; the next inner layer correspondentially is the firmament as a containant.
Introduces the next identifications (vessels, darkness, gall, intestines).
Gall corresponds to bitter ruling motive; “ruler” keeps the cosmological register rather than moralizing.
“breadth of the great … of the worlds” corresponds to a great expanse: firmament.
Eyes in cosmic-man schemata commonly map to sun and moon; fits “channels of circulation” nearby and the substrate cosmography.
Feet already mapped; “His feet are his …” naturally completes with “soles” as the ultimate surface.
Introduces the inference from the cosmic body description to the equilibrium statement.
“Five gods are fastened in him. In them…” continues to what those five are within this structure.
Links: “they are his soul and his life; also man is a sinner…”
Sets the contrast: man is a sinner, yet the Living Spirit and Ambassador and guardians are present as ordering powers.
Opens the list of overseers placed over the cosmic structure: Keeper of Splendour etc.
Matches the fixed-in-camp motif; these powers are stationed and fixed.
The mind above is described in the substrate as a stored realm of light or treasure. “Treasury” keeps impersonal cosmological diction.
Required article before “whole … of the powers…”.
Powers of heaven are “in the camp of the great King of Honour”.

fills.fill: who is the thought that exists i

fills.notes: King of Honour’s station is repeatedly the third firmament in this chapter; restoring that location keeps internal consistency.

Adamant of Light is typically stationed higher than the third and associated with firm stability; placing it in a higher firmament preserves the ordered descent (7th thought, then adamant insight, then glory counsel, then porter consideration).
Completes: “from … he has given …” as distribution to that power.
King of Glory = counsel and patience; “counsel and patience” is the pairing used later in the chapter (new man’s counsel=patience).
King of Glory is given charge “over the three images” and receives authority to restrain evils so they do not act.
In ¶22 he rules the three wheels and the ascent-paths are impeded; here he is handed the administration of those paths.
Introduces the next appointment: the Porter.
“He has … the Porter” needs the verb “appointed”.

fills.fill: and the wisdom in the place
fills.notes: Porter corresponds to consideration and wisdom in the lowest region; restores the doctrinal mapping.
Foundation below corresponds to the lowest plane under the three earths, consistent with ¶23 and ¶28.
The strengthening is by fixed ordinances so each province remains secure—impersonal substrate term.
Keeps the sequence: treachery, uprising, Sin aborts, tangles, mixes, then moves and insinuates; “and it was” bridges to the next action.
Restores “watch-tower of the Keeper of Splendour.”
“He is made … with wrath” needs the infinitive idea: thought turned toward nothingness or negation; but here the phrase is idiomatic: “made full of wrath.” Next lacuna provides “full”.
The sentence requires a consequence clause: “A destruction, on the earth … to it.” The spiritual translation says “disturbance and destruction…”.
Identifies Adamant’s function as insight, matching the fivefold mapping later (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration).

fills.fill: n the camp of the Adamant
fills.notes: Restores “set firm upon …” as his camp or station.
Needs an adverb modifying “pained and oppressed”.
“paths closed to their …” corresponds to ways or passages for ascent.
Introduces the result clause about ascent impeded.
Corresponds to “uprising of the abysses below”.
Sets up: “bent, the fastenings underneath were loosened”.
Completes the earthquake effect in the foundation below.
“as it … helper” needs “became a helper”.
The descent of Jesus in this chapter is consistently “Jesus the Youth” (¶17); the oldest layer keeps the functional title.
Connects “he sent Jesus … the prayer of the five sons.”
“He assumed them … the abortions” requires “from among”.
“fastenings that …” requires a prior fixing: bindings that had been set beneath were loosened.
“up to his own rest” is the expected closure in this descent-and-return pattern.
Completes: gods master, “watching over them in their appointed places.”
Matches the repeated motif: uprisings, treachery, earthquake in watches.

fills.fill: it at once, and bind it, since
fills.notes: Spiritual logic: evil is permitted briefly, then seized and judged; the text needs the seizing/binding action before “they have acted first with a righteous judgement.”

fills.fill: are set in their camps, though they
fills.notes: Explains how great beings can be present in bounded places: they are stationed and yet confined.
“bearing up till …” naturally closes with endurance until completion: “till the end.”
These powers “pronouncing… continually leading”; the missing verb describes their constant insinuation.
“worshipping the things that … will not remain” needs “are in the world” as the transient objects.
“making obeisance to idols”
Completes the idol list: wood, gold, silver, and stone; standard substrate polemic without Christian overlay.
Restores the movement: forgets, does not know how to pray, becomes hostile.
Old substrate often speaks of two sources (father and mother) as higher principles; here it matches “father … itself” and remaining light within.
Corresponds to turning against its own remaining light.
“finds the soul … it assuming it” needs the state: the soul is found in bonds.
He assumes it “in the body” as the locus of bondage.
Introduces “by his wisdom”.
Introduces the result: he becomes for it…
He becomes “power over the bonds” and members.

fills.fill: mind of the soul and relea

fills.notes: After adding his word, what is received becomes “nourisher and strengthener”; the substrate term paired with “word” here is “utterance”.
Completes: “so that his utterance of the new man becomes nourisher…”
The process is brought to fullness “and perfect also the twelve members” (twelve as fullness of organized truths).
Introduces the description of the righteous state as he perfects the whole.
“and his wisdom. His … becomes righteous” needs “mind”: mind and wisdom as the interior pair being rectified.
Repeats the completion statement to close the clause.
Formerly running in disorder; spiritual translation: ran in track of disorder.
Now runs in ordered way.
“his road and his path and his ascent”.
Ascent results in conjunction with higher aeons or communities.
Old man bound “in the body” as ultimate restraint.
Triad: lust, craft, foolishness.
Completes the sentence: “in these five members of the body …”
“Yet, his king is the Light Mind”
“While the members …, thus sin is imprisoned” requires the fixing of the members in order.
Parallel to “foolish words”: foolish deeds arising from clouded understanding.
“confusion… in the zone… Again… disturbance… in the camps of the Light Mind” matches the structural mapping of provinces.
“for they are set as firm…”
Core point: great powers “contorted themselves” by accommodation; “bent themselves down” is the substrate phrasing.
Completes the comparison: as pure gods are not defiled in mingling, so the Light Mind is not defiled while placed in the fleshly body.

assessment: Most lacunae are trivial letter-restorations and are secure. The substantial gaps cluster in the cosmic-body catalogue (¶11–12) and the appointment list (¶14); there the correspondential structure constrains functions (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration; discrete degrees; stations in firmaments), but exact cosmographic nouns are sometimes only tentatively recoverable. Where the spiritual translation fixed a required relation (ascent-paths, confinement in camps, seizing and binding after permission), restorations are strong to moderate; where the manuscript likely had detailed technical terms for zones, seas, skins, vessels, and firmaments, confidence drops to tentative.
